questions.q: Three vectors $\vec{a}, \vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ are such that $|\vec{a}| = 1, |\vec{b}| = 2$ and $|\vec{c}| = 4$ along with $\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c} = 0$. Then, the value of $4\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + 3\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} + 3\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}$ will be
questions.solution:
Given $\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c} = 0$

Squaring both sides, we get:

$|\vec{a}|^2 + |\vec{b}|^2 + |\vec{c}|^2 + 2(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} + \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}) = 0$

Substituting the given magnitudes $|\vec{a}| = 1$, $|\vec{b}| = 2$, and $|\vec{c}| = 4$:

$1^2 + 2^2 + 4^2 + 2(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} + \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}) = 0$

$21 + 2(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} + \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}) = 0$

$\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} + \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a} = -\dfrac{21}{2}$

From the given equation, we can also write:

$\vec{a} + \vec{b} = -\vec{c}$

Squaring both sides:

$|\vec{a}|^2 + |\vec{b}|^2 + 2\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = |\vec{c}|^2$

$1^2 + 2^2 + 2\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = 4^2$

$5 + 2\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = 16$

$2\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = 11 \Rightarrow \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = \dfrac{11}{2}$

The expression to be evaluated is $4\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + 3\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} + 3\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}$, which can be rewritten as:

$\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + 3(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} + \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a})$

Substituting the obtained values:

$\dfrac{11}{2} + 3\left(-\dfrac{21}{2}\right) = \dfrac{11 - 63}{2} = -\dfrac{52}{2} = -26$

Answer: $-26$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If a vector $\vec{v} = 3\hat{i}$ is rotated in the $x - z$ plane by an angle $\theta$ with respect to x-axis in the clockwise direction, then for an observer at +y axis the vector will be
questions.solution:
For an observer on the $+y$ axis looking towards the origin, the normal to the plane of observation is $\hat{j}$.

By the right-hand rule, a counter-clockwise rotation in the $x-z$ plane corresponds to curling fingers from the $+z$ axis to the $+x$ axis (since $\hat{k} \times \hat{i} = \hat{j}$).

Therefore, a clockwise rotation is in the opposite direction, from the $+x$ axis towards the $+z$ axis.

The initial vector is $\vec{v} = 3\hat{i}$, which lies along the $+x$ axis.

When it is rotated clockwise by an angle $\theta$, it moves towards the $+z$ axis. The new vector will have a positive $x$-component and a positive $z$-component.

From the geometry, the component along the $x$-axis becomes $3\cos\theta$ and the component along the $z$-axis becomes $3\sin\theta$.

Thus, the rotated vector is $\vec{v}' = 3\cos\theta\hat{i} + 3\sin\theta\hat{k}$.

Answer: $3\cos\theta\hat{i} + 3\sin\theta\hat{k}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The density of the material of a cube can be estimated by measuring its mass and the length of one of its sides. If the maximum error in the measurement of mass and length are $0.3 \%$ and $0.2 \%$ respectively, the maximum error in the estimation of the density of the cube is approximately.
questions.solution:
Given,
Maximum error in the measurement of mass $=0.3 \%$
Maximum error in the measurement of length $=0.2 \%$
We know that,
Error in density is given as,
$\text {Density, } \rho=\frac{\text { mass }(m)}{\text { volume }(V)}=\frac{m}{L^{3}}$
where, $L=$ side of cube
Error in density is given as,
$\left(\frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho}\right)=\frac{\Delta m}{m}+\frac{3 \Delta L}{L}$
or $\left(\frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho}\right) \times 100=\left(\frac{\Delta m}{m}+\frac{3 \Delta L}{L}\right) \times 100$
Substituting the given values, we get
$\left(\frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho}\right)_{\max }=(0.3 \%+3(0.2) \%=0.3 \%+0.6 \%\therefore$ Maximum percentage error measurement of density $\left(\frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho}\right)_{\max }=0.9 \%$

&=\alpha(\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2 \hat{k})+\beta(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}) \\
